transcript: Conceptualize and envision the dissociation of H2 in phase space.
narrative: In **phase space (z, p_z)**, the dissociation of **H₂** unfolds not as an unphysical static matrix collapse, but as continuous kinetic transport of the one-particle reduced density matrix. At equilibrium (R = 0.74 Å), the electronic Wigner distribution forms a single coherent quantum droplet concentrated in the inter-nuclear bonding valley. As the bond stretches toward R = 1.60 Å—traversing the critical **Coulson-Fischer point (R ≈ 1.20 Å)**—conventional mean-field theory suffers a topological bifurcation, artificially breaking spin symmetry. In Q-BOLTZ phase space, the **kinetic collision operator** regularizes this singularity into a smooth, deterministic transport: the Wigner fluid bifurcates into two entangled, symmetric droplets centered at each proton (`z = ±R/2, p_z = 0`). The active-space natural occupations relax smoothly to `[1.9182, 0.0818]` with an informational entropy of **0.9857 bits** and total energy of **-22.8415 eV**, seamlessly recovering the Generalized Valence Bond (GVB) limit with exact spin purity.
